headline: Pretrained sequence models extend to nucleic acids and ligands, while benchmarks expose generalization gaps
label: Sequence Foundation Model Reliability
summary: New benchmarks on MET kinase inhibitors and protein-RNA interfaces test whether pretrained sequence and structure models generalize beyond their training distributions.
synthesis: Pretrained representations are being adapted across modalities: structRFM on 21M RNA sequence-structure pairs, IsoAlign with JEPA objectives for isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment, PDLMs on paired protein-DNA sequences, PALM (ESM2 with LoRA and BiLSTM), MaskNGly for zero-shot N-glycosylation, and AtomLM-9b for all-atom structure tokenization. The evaluation findings are the more notable development. On MET kinase deep mutational scans across 11 inhibitors, models are largely ligand-invariant, indicating they miss inhibitor-specific effects. RPFace pairs a small sequence-only model with a stratified protein-RNA interface benchmark that exposes biases in existing structural benchmarks. The RNA-small molecule review likewise organizes evaluation by binding site, preference, and pose tasks. The emphasis is shifting from architecture scale toward stratified, ligand-aware testing.
